svg.title: A PlanRequest on the time line
svg.desc: Animated: how Dispatch (central package) fills each PlanRequest field from the schedule it is running, what it expects back, and why, with today's settings, base_schedule and active_jobs are always empty.
svg.metadata: ["The schedule Dispatch is running when its planner timer fires. Each box is one ActionNode on the lane of the asset that executes it. Faded boxes are completed. The line marks now.", "id is a fresh Guid that the response must echo. base_state is GetLatest(): Dispatch's own copy of the garage, advanced by completion events. AGV-2 has lifted T15 at P15 (a0 is done).", "base_schedule is every action not yet completed (a1, a2, a3, b1), with parent indices renumbered. Dispatch also has a split (SplitSchedule, a 30 s command horizon, outside_split), but the call is commented out, so nothing is held back.", "active_jobs is every job in Dispatch's jobs_active_ list: the jobs those actions belong to (J-A and J-B). planned_jobs is never filled by Dispatch.", "pending_jobs: queued jobs that pass ShouldPendingJobBePlanned, in queue order, capped by the current request strategy. They have no actions yet.", "What Dispatch expects back: every base_schedule node, unchanged, plus the new nodes with parents pointing into them. It rebuilds its schedule from the response alone. Today's scheduler reserves AGV-2 and B21 and returns only n1..n5, so Dispatch would reject this response.", "What happens today: enable_overlapping_planning_ is false and no parameter sets it, so ShouldCallPlanner refuses while any job is active. Plan() runs only after J-A and J-B finish, with an empty base_schedule and empty active_jobs."]
